citation.sourceDocument: Washington Department of Revenue, no personal income tax on wages (a separate 7% capital-gains excise tax applies to certain high earners)
citation.sourceNote: A state with no income tax is a first-class record here, not an omission: the shard exists, carries a citation, and answers "nothing" deliberately rather than by having nothing to say. The caveat that matters is what a $0 state income tax does NOT mean. A state still has to fund itself, and the ones without an income tax generally lean harder on sales and property taxes — neither of which this engine models. So a take-home figure here is exactly right about state income tax and silent about the rest of the state's tax burden; comparing two states on this number alone will mislead you. Washington levies no individual income tax on WAGES, and Art. VII of the Washington Constitution as construed by the state Supreme Court has long been read to bar a graduated one. Since 2022 it has levied a 7% EXCISE TAX on long-term capital gains above an inflation-adjusted standard deduction (roughly $270,000 for 2024), upheld by the state Supreme Court in 2023 as an excise rather than an income tax. That is a real tax on a real gain and it is not modeled here: this engine is wage-based, so a Washington filer with a large stock sale owes more than any figure on this site shows. Washington also has no personal exemption or standard deduction to model, and a high combined sales tax.
